title: B-score: Detecting biases in large language models using response history

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the over-selection of specific digits or numbers (e.g., the number 7) in multiple-choice and generation tasks by comparing single-turn vs. multi-turn response probabilities (B-score).
Comparing answer probabilities in single-turn vs. multi-turn settings (B-score) on multiple-choice questions regarding gender associations (e.g., gender of a mathematician).
Evaluating single-turn and multi-turn selection frequencies for political figures (e.g., Trump vs. Biden) in subjective and factual queries to compute the B-score.

Calculating the B-score based on single-turn vs. multi-turn probability differences when models select racial groups for hypothetical scenarios (e.g., CEO of a tech company), as well as evaluating on the BBQ benchmark.
Evaluating LLM preferences for specific countries in subjective and factual multiple-choice questions using the B-score metric.
Assessing arbitrary preference for specific names in multiple-choice questions by comparing single-turn and multi-turn response distributions.
Measuring bias towards or against certain professions in subjective and factual multiple-choice questions using the B-score.
Detecting arbitrary preferences for specific sports teams or clubs by comparing single-turn and multi-turn response probabilities.

bias_targets.target: Miscellaneous Social Biases (Age, Disability, Religion, Socio-economic, Sexual orientation, Physical appearance)
bias_targets.methodology: Applying the B-score metric (difference between single-turn and multi-turn answer probabilities) to ambiguous multiple-choice questions from the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA) dataset.
